records.title: Promise: Predictive and Cost-Optimal Migrations for Service-Continuous Edge Intelligence in Multi-UAV Networks
records.venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)

identity_evidence.quote: Promise: Predictive and Cost-Optimal Migrations for Service-Continuous Edge Intelligence in Multi-UAV Networks

primary_full_report.rationale: Primary 9-page IEEE ICWS conference paper (pp. 488–496) presenting the Promise schema, LST-GNN prediction, MINLP formulation, NP-hardness proofs, PDBH algorithm, and simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: To achieve the service-continuous edge intelligence, we propose a predictive and cost-optimal migration scheme, named Promise, through jointly optimizing across-swarm UAV migration and intra-swarm service migration.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section VII-A simulates three UAV swarms deployed in a monitoring area containing 5, 10, and 15 UAVs (30 UAVs total) coordinated with a ground control station.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The three swarms are arranged in an equilateral triangular topology with a side length of 100 m, where the numbers of UAVs in the three swarms are set to 5, 10, and 15, respectively.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Sections II, III, and VII-A model and evaluate partitioning each ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 inference task into sequential task modules distributed across different UAVs within a swarm, with predictive and failure-recovery intra-swarm service migration and cross-swarm UAV migration.
collaborative_inference.quote: Each generated task is equally partition into two task modules, which are distributed to different UAVs within the same swarm using the Greedy allocation algorithm.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section VII reports server-based simulation experiments comparing Promise against NPG, THR-G, LSTM-P, and DTASM under 20, 40, and 80 tasks/time-slot and random UAV failures on task success rate, migration cost, and ResNet-18 inference accuracy.
evaluative_evidence.quote: Considering the cost and complexity of real-world large-scale deployment, simulation experiments are performed to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed Promise. The experiments are conducted on a server equipped with an Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12600KF CPU at 3.70 GHz and 32 GB RAM

records.title: Orion: A Collaborative Edge Inference Framework for Large Language Models Processing Multi-Sensor Data in UAV Swarms

identity_evidence.quote: Orion: A Collaborative Edge Inference Framework for Large Language Models Processing Multi-Sensor Data in UAV Swarms

primary_full_report.rationale: Primary 26-page peer-reviewed MDPI Drones original research article presenting the Orion framework, Algorithms 1–2, theoretical boundary analyses, and comprehensive simulation evaluations.
primary_full_report.quote: Motivated by these gaps, we propose Orion, a novel collaborative inference framework for sensor-aware LLM deployment at the edge.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section 4.1 and Table 1 (p. 15) specify that the evaluated simulation models a four-UAV swarm (3 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin UAV nodes and 1 NVIDIA Orin NX UAV node) interconnected via inter-UAV ad hoc links (400–1000 Mb/s), with Orion partitioning Llama-2 inference across those simulated UAV nodes.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: UAV node (3 units) NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (1.88 TFLOPS, 16 GB RAM) UAV node (1 unit) NVIDIA Orin NX (3.33 TFLOPS, 32 GB RAM)

collaborative_inference.rationale: Section 3 specifies edge-only collaborative LLM inference across UAV swarm nodes using dynamic-programming layer partitioning, adaptive sequence partitioning, and speculative first-token predictive decoding across pipeline stages.
collaborative_inference.quote: Orion incorporates three innovations: (1) optimal model partitioning via dynamic programming, (2) adaptive sequence partitioning that balances causal attention load across pipeline stages, and (3) a predictive decoding mechanism that speculatively generates the first token during idle intervals.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section 4 evaluates Orion in a Python 3.13.5 simulation framework against five baselines across Llama-2 7B/13B/70B, varying sequence lengths and bandwidths, ablation variants, break-even predictive decoding Monte Carlo trials, and noise-injection sensitivity runs.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We implemented a comprehensive simulation framework in Python 3.13.5 to evaluate Orion’s performance rigorously. Our custom simulation accurately models UAV onboard capabilities, such as compute performance and memory capacity. It also captures aerial ad hoc network characteristics, including bandwidth and latency.

date_window.rationale: Page 1 explicitly records publication on 26 May 2026, within the 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25 window.
date_window.quote: Received: 17 April 2026 Revised: 15 May 2026 Accepted: 21 May 2026 Published: 26 May 2026

english.quote: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms generate massive multi-modal sensor data streams from onboard payloads such as RGB cameras, LiDAR, and thermal sensors. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret these data for natural language-based swarm coordination.

alignment.rationale: Core contribution is joint layer-to-UAV pipeline partitioning (Algorithm 1) and adaptive input sequence chunk partitioning (Algorithm 2) with speculative first-token prediction across heterogeneous UAV onboard nodes.
alignment.quote: To address the aforementioned challenges, we propose Orion, an edge-only collaborative inference framework specifically optimized for UAV swarms.

unresolved: Evaluation relies on a Python 3.13.5 simulation with theoretically derived per-layer latency coefficients (Section 3.2.1, p. 10) and simulated sensor traces rather than physical Jetson cluster execution or physical UAV flight tests (deferred to Section 5.5, p. 23).

records.title: Multi-Agent Meta Reinforcement Learning for Reliable and Low-Latency Distributed Inference in Resource-Constrained UAV Swarms

primary_full_report.quote: To address these issues, we formulate the problem of CNN layer distribution and UAV trajectory planning (LDTP) as an optimization problem to improve latency, reliability, and resource usage.

multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The simulation began with five UAVs in the swarm, and notably, the MARL-meta algorithm quickly converged with higher accuracy and lower latency compared to traditional DRL algorithms.

collaborative_inference.quote: After receiving the data, each UAV processes its respective layer(s) and forwards the intermediate results to the next UAV, which continues the process until the final output is generated.

evaluative_evidence.quote: In this section, we present the simulation results that assess the performance of our proposed solutions. We employed Windows core i7, with 4 cores, an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.2 GHz and 16 GB RAM to run the simulation experiments.

records.title: A LINK-LAYER MODEL OF A UAV SWARM MESH NETWORK WITH ENCAPSULATION OF INTERMEDIATE DEEP NEURAL NETWORK ACTIVATIONS: ANALYTICAL EVALUATION OF LATENCY AND TRAFFIC VOLUME
records.venue: Information and communication technologies, electronic engineering

identity_evidence.quote: A LINK-LAYER MODEL OF A UAV SWARM MESH NETWORK WITH ENCAPSULATION OF INTERMEDIATE DEEP NEURAL NETWORK ACTIVATIONS: ANALYTICAL EVALUATION OF LATENCY AND TRAFFIC VOLUME

primary_full_report.rationale: Primary 11-page peer-reviewed journal article (pp. 144–154) proposing the SwarmNS-MAC link-layer frame encapsulation model, 24-byte TLV header, three-phase collective inference algorithm, and analytical latency/traffic/quorum model.
primary_full_report.quote: This paper proposes a link-layer model of a UAV swarm mesh network, SwarmNS-MAC, in which IEEE 802.11 frames serve as direct containers for quantized fragments of intermediate DNN activations.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section 3 (p. 4) models a multi-UAV swarm graph G(t) = (V, E(t)) where UAV nodes V compute local split-DNN layers (1..k) and transmit intermediate activation tensors to an aggregator node collecting from neighbors N(i). Under Protocol Section 4.1(4) and Amendment 001, mathematical performance studies are eligible evaluation methods and neither network simulation nor executed DNNs are required; Section 6 connects that multi-UAV architecture to numerical evaluation by setting n = 6 aggregator neighbors (Table 2, p. 6) and computing binomial aggregation quorum probabilities (Eq. (7), p. 6; pp. 7–8, Fig. 3) from single-hop per-link tensor delivery (Table 3, p. 7). The single-hop and analytical assumptions disclosed on pp. 8–9 (Table 4, Section 7) are quality-appraisal and synthesis limitations rather than a failure of multi-UAV eligibility.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The swarm is represented by a dynamic graph G(t) = (V, E(t)), where V is the set of UAVs, and E(t) is the set of bidirectional radio links, which changes due to mobility.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Sections 3–5 formalize split DNN inference across UAV swarm nodes computing local layers 1..k, quantizing and encapsulating intermediate activation tensors into L2 frames, and executing final layers at an aggregator with quorum-based graceful degradation.
collaborative_inference.quote: In the split computing paradigm, a deep neural network (DNN) is partitioned among swarm nodes, so that instead of raw imagery the nodes exchange intermediate activation tensors

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Sections 5–6 provide an analytical mathematical performance model and numerical evaluation for a 256×80×80 YOLO-like activation tensor comparing L2 SwarmNS-MAC against L2–L7 across FP32, INT8, and 0.8-bit quantization, effective link speeds, tensor delivery probability, and quorum probability.
evaluative_evidence.quote: The calculations were performed for a reference feature tensor of dimensions 256×80×80 (1,638,400 elements), typical for the intermediate layers of YOLO-family object detectors with a 640×640 input image.

records.title: A cognitive synergetic hierarchical framework for UAV swarm combat via speculative inference and role-decoupled reinforcement learning

identity_evidence.quote: A cognitive synergetic hierarchical framework for UAV swarm combat via speculative inference and role-decoupled reinforcement learning

primary_full_report.rationale: Primary 22-page peer-reviewed Original Research article in Frontiers in Neurorobotics presenting the Brain–Torso cognitive synergetic framework, mathematical proofs, JSBSim simulation setup, ablation studies, and case studies.
primary_full_report.quote: We bridge this gap by introducing a cognitive synergetic hierarchical framework that decouples strategic reasoning from tactical execution. Our architecture splits the workload between a “Strategic Brain” and a “Tactical Torso.”

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Section 5 evaluates multi-UAV swarms in 2v2 heterogeneous cooperation (Scenario B), 6v6 swarm combat with jammers (Scenario C), and 4v4 and 8v8 scalability experiments in JSBSim.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: To see if our architecture actually gives a tactical edge, we ran our Brain-Torso setup against five baselines in Scenario B (2v2 coordination) and Scenario C (6v6 scale combat; scenario specifics are outlined in Section 5.1.2).

collaborative_inference.rationale: Sections 4.5.2, 4.6.2, and 5.3 implement and evaluate runtime cloud-to-edge speculative LLM inference (7B draft model on UAV Jetson AGX Orin verified in parallel by 70B target model on ground station, with autonomous-edge fallback under link flapping) plus intra-swarm sequential intention propagation (SIP) across UAV agents.
collaborative_inference.quote: For the Brain, we utilize a synergy between DeepSeek-R1 (70B) and its 7B distilled counterpart to create a collaborative inference engine.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Section 5 evaluates the system using JSBSim 6-DOF combat simulation coupled with dual-RTX 3090 (70B) and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (7B + MAPPO Actor) hardware across six baselines, cross-play opponents, communication disruptions, and four ablations.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We moved away from simplistic point-mass models (Imado et al., 2011; Kinoshita and Imado, 2006) and instead built our environment on the JSBSim flight dynamics engine to capture the true nuances of aerial combat.
